parts.text: Which claim best explains why the immersed bottle feels lighter?

options.text: The water applies an upward force on the bottle equal to the weight of the water the bottle displaces.
The water removes the downward pull of Earth on the bottle.
The mass of the bottle decreases while it is in the water.
The water applies only a downward force on the bottle.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Dev lowers a closed empty plastic bottle into a bucket of water. The bottle feels lighter in the water than in the air, and it tends to bounce upward.

part_answers.answer: Immersed objects feel lighter because the liquid pushes up with a buoyant force equal to the weight of the liquid displaced.

teacher.key_rationale: Buoyancy is an upward force from the liquid equal to the weight of displaced liquid. Claiming Earth stops pulling, mass falls, or the liquid only pushes down all miss that hinge.
